questions.category: A1 — Apply Shop and Site Safety Practices
questions.question: Before starting work on a jobsite, what is the first thing a carpenter should do?
options: Identify hazards and review safe work procedures
questions.explanation: Hazard identification comes before work begins. It helps prevent injuries. Safe procedures must be understood before using tools or materials.

questions.question: Which PPE is most important when cutting lumber with a circular saw?
questions.explanation: Cutting creates flying chips and loud noise. Eye and hearing protection are required. PPE must match the hazard.

questions.category: B1 — Use Construction Drawings and Specifications
questions.question: On construction drawings, dimensions are usually taken from:
questions.explanation: Written dimensions take priority over scaling. Scaling can be inaccurate due to printing. Always follow noted dimensions.

questions.category: B2 — Interpret Building Codes and Bylaws
questions.question: The main purpose of a building code is to:
options: Set minimum safety and performance requirements
questions.explanation: Building codes establish minimum standards. They protect life safety, health, and structural performance. Codes are legally enforceable.

questions.question: Which action best shows good job planning?
options: Review drawings, sequence work, and prepare materials
questions.explanation: Planning reduces mistakes and delays. A carpenter should understand the task before starting. Proper sequencing improves efficiency.
